Plagiarism. The University defines this as the practice of presenting the thoughts, writings or other output of another or others as original, without acknowledgement of their source(s) at the point of their use in the student’s work.
Falsification or fabrication of data. The University defines this as the misrepresentation of the results of experimental work or the presentation of fictitious results.
Any student who assists a fellow student, or student(s), to commit misconduct shall be deemed to have committed misconduct and will be dealt with in accordance with the Student Conduct Procedure.

Personation. The University defines this as a substitute taking the place of a student in an examination, preparing coursework for assessment on behalf of another student, or submitting coursework for assessment that has been prepared by someone other than the student to whom the resulting grade would be attributed.

Cheating. The University defines this (in relation to examinations) as the taking of any unauthorised material (hardcopy or electronic) into an examination; the unauthorised use of technology in examinations

detection.quote: the Dean shall have discretion to question the student on various aspects of the work, including the methods used to produce the work, key sources underpinning the work and the student’s knowledge of the subject area.
Preliminary Investigating Officer may exceptionally request specific information to inform their consideration, e.g. submission of draft work within 24 hours.

process.quote: Where academic misconduct is suspected, the Dean shall be informed in the first instance, including where it relates to the University’s student accommodation.
the Dean shall appoint a Preliminary Investigating Officer who will review the Academic Misconduct Referral Form, the accompanying evidence and recommendation made by the Reporter.
The student shall be given every opportunity to explain the circumstances of the case and to submit any relevant evidence of extenuating circumstances for consideration.
arrange a Misconduct Hearing with the student at the earliest possible opportunity, and normally not later than 10 working days after the allegation has been received by the Dean;
If the student fails to attend without providing a good reason for nonattendance, then the meeting will proceed in their absence, without this constituting grounds for appeal.
advising of their entitlement to be accompanied by two persons (who should not be materially involved), to call witnesses, and that the Student Union may be contacted for advice and support;
A student shall be entitled to submit an appeal: (i) against the decision and/or the sanction(s) (though not replacement costs) if a Dean has determined misconduct has been established;
The student shall submit the Student Appeal Form: Misconduct to their Dean within 10 working days of the student receiving notification of the outcome.
on the basis that the standard of proof to be used when allegations of misconduct are investigated shall be the balance of probabilities.
The Academic Quality Team shall maintain a central record of all misconduct cases and sanction(s) and report these annually to Academic Council.

outcomes.quote: Mandatory Education/Training: Participation at a relevant internal and/or external education/awareness programme (e.g. mental health, drug, alcohol), or other constructive activity.
Reprimand: Written warning, retained by the Dean in the School’s student file.

Grades for the individual component of assessment affected by the academic misconduct be reduced to Grade F or equivalent, and the student be permitted the remaining re-assessment attempts as would normally apply to that component of assessment.

Revocation of previously-conferred award: A recommendation to the Principal (via the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic)) to revoke an award

definitions.quote: False Authorship. The University defines this as the practice of submitting work where the student is not the author of that work.

Plagiarism. The University defines this as the practice of presenting the thoughts, writings or other output of another or others as original, without acknowledgement of their source(s) at the point of their use in the student’s work.
Falsification or fabrication of data. The University defines this as the misrepresentation of the results of experimental work or the presentation of fictitious results.

Collusion. The University defines this as two or more students working together, without the prior authorisation of the Course Leader, tutor or supervisor, to produce the same piece of work, and then attempting to present this work as their own.
Bribery. The University defines this as the paying, offering or attempted exchange of an inducement for information or material intended to advantage the recipient in an assessment.

Personation. The University defines this as a substitute taking the place of a student in an examination, preparing coursework for assessment on behalf of another student, or submitting coursework for assessment that has been prepared by someone other than the student to whom the resulting grade would be attributed.
Academic misconduct is defined by the University as any attempt by a student(s) to affect an unfair advantage in any assessment
